headline: Philippines summons Chinese ambassador over 'easily win' remarks
dek: Foreign Secretary Ma. sources: Associated Press; Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs official statement (facebook.com/dfaphl, verified, 1.4M followers)
fault_line: Expel the ambassador and draw a red line — vs — the 'threat' is overhyped and expulsion would wreck a vital economic relationship. Who is bluffing: Beijing or Manila?

sections.what_happened: Foreign Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro summoned Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan Monday to convey 'serious concern and strong objection' to his Oct 15 remarks that China 'may easily win' a conflict with the Philippines — Manila calls it a threat of the use of force, 'provocative and unacceptable'; DFA reserves right to further diplomatic action; China backs its envoy, FM spokesperson Mao Ning calls the reaction an overreaction and tells Manila to 'rein in' politicians. At least two Philippine senators demanded expulsion/persona non grata; palace Oct 19 said Marcos has not signaled intent to expel.
sections.what_verified: AP wire carried by khaosodenglish, dailyexcelsior, dtnext, newswav; DFA's own official statement with photos of the summoning; Jing Quan's own remarks reported consistently (Diliman Dialogues, Oct 15, responding to Defense Secretary Teodoro's 'troublemaker' label).
sections.what_disputed: Chinese embassy (Manila, Friday): remarks were taken out of context via 'selective quotation and overinterpretation'; Jing Quan Monday evening (embassy FB): 'despite our capacity, we don't have the intention to use force... there is no need to resort to force.' China MFA backs the envoy.
sections.why_matters: The split, not the bloc: China's 'we love peace' mask slips the moment a US treaty ally pushes back — the same week China courts Iran and mediates. Is 'easily win' a threat or a confession of intent? Map explainer: the SCS flashpoints behind the words.
sections.context: Background: Philippines summons Chinese ambassador over 'easily win' remarks — NEW Monday (South China Sea/Taiwan fault line)
